questions.stem: A $12 \mathrm{~V}$ battery connected to a coil of resistance $6 \Omega$ through a switch, drives a constant current in the circuit. The switch is opened in $1 \mathrm{~ms}$. The emf induced across the coil is $20 \mathrm{~V}$. The inductance of the coil is :
questions.solution: The initial steady current is $I=V/R=12/6=2\,\mathrm A$. Using the stated switch-off interval, $|\mathcal E|=L\Delta I/\Delta t$, hence $L=20(10^{-3})/2=0.010\,\mathrm H=10\,\mathrm{mH}$.

questions.stem: A conducting loop of radius $\frac{10}{\sqrt{\pi}} \mathrm{cm}$ is placed perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of $0.5 T$. The magnetic field is decreased to zero in $0.5 s$ at a steady rate. The induced emf in the circular loop at $0.25 s$ is:
questions.solution: The loop area is $\pi(0.10/\sqrt{\pi})^2=0.01\,\mathrm{m^2}$. The magnitude of the rate of change of field is $0.5/0.5=1\,\mathrm{T\,s^{-1}}$. Faraday's law gives $|\mathcal E|=A|dB/dt|=0.01\,\mathrm V=10\,\mathrm{mV}$ throughout the steady decrease.
